mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistent across multiple economic cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that reduces corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the directional accuracy falls below 55% over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The interaction effect is stronger than either series alone.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression of SPX 20d returns on the interaction term, or the directional accuracy is below 55% over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a rising federal funds rate above 2.5% for two consecutive months compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles, or the regime-specific directional accuracy is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200 thousand units for two consecutive months, it indicates a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 1200, or the directional accuracy is below 55% over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an overheating economy with tight labor markets, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated rate hikes and inflation concerns.
failure_condition: The interaction term is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression, or the directional accuracy of the interaction signal is below 55% over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle supply shocks, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.5 for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate output.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods classified as late-cycle supply shocks, or the regime-specific directional accuracy is below 55%.
